races.name: GAIN Equine Nutrition Irish European Breeders Fund Fillies Maiden

runners_data.name: Alpha
runners_data.comment: Outstanding breeding — her dam a multiple Group 1 winner — gives Alpha every reason to be exciting; a debut second at Leopardstown, beaten ¾ lengths while showing early inexperience, showed she can handle the trip and will improve. The stable has landed this race in three consecutive runnings and she is well placed to build on that experience.

runners_data.name: Alreem
runners_data.comment: A 230,000 euros Starman filly from a yard with a strong first-time-out record; her dam was very useful at extended distances and successful on her second start, which at least provides a stamina foundation. A significant purchase making her debut, and the market will be the best guide.

runners_data.name: Endless Night
runners_data.comment: A full sister to Thesecretadversary — high-class at 7f — and by St Mark's Basilica out of a smart middle-distance mare, giving Endless Night outstanding credentials for this trip and beyond. The stable is capable of producing debutants ready to run and the market is worth watching.

runners_data.name: Exceptionally
runners_data.comment: A half-sister to City Of Troy and by Into Mischief out of a Group 1-winning dam; the pedigree is formidable, though the stronger claims in this race appear to lie with a stablemate. The market will be instructive; the stable has landed this race in each of the last three runnings.

runners_data.name: Exchange Student
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on debut at Listowel, showing clear inexperience throughout without landing a blow; she needs to demonstrate significant improvement today and is firmly on the outside of the market on our figures. Bred to prefer a sound surface and there is scope, but she has plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Ibelieveicanfly
runners_data.comment: An encouraging 2¼-length fourth on debut at Leopardstown in a competitive maiden, seemingly knowing her job from the outset with considerably more in reserve; her dam is a French Listed winner and she is bred to stay at least 10f. The stable has landed this race three runnings in a row and she rates the chief danger here.

runners_data.name: Isle Of Capri
runners_data.comment: Wootton Bassett filly out of a dam who was very useful at 8f and herself went very close on debut; jockey bookings suggest this is the stable's first string here. There is limited guide beyond breeding and market, but the dam's profile is encouraging for today's trip.

runners_data.name: Littlepacer
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on debut at Leopardstown, failing to make any impression and clearly showing inexperience throughout; she has speed on the sire's side and some stamina through the dam. Ranked last of 13 on our figures, she has plenty to demonstrate before being taken seriously here.

runners_data.name: Livenka
runners_data.comment: Finished with a strong late run on debut at Naas, third beaten 2½ lengths after a slow start; she should have learnt considerably from that outing and is likely to improve. Acts on good ground and rates a serious danger if her stamina over today's trip is confirmed.

runners_data.name: Old Joanie
runners_data.comment: A 38,000 euros State Of Rest filly and a half-sister to Devoirs Choice, very useful at 8f; her dam was effective at 6f as a juvenile and successful over 12f, giving a wide stamina range. The rivals here set a strong standard and she rates one to watch carefully.

runners_data.name: Pretty Thoughts
runners_data.comment: A modestly bred debutante by Gregorian out of an unraced dam, from a stable with a strong reputation in point-to-point circles; this is unfamiliar territory for that yard and there is little to go on beyond pedigree. One to observe rather than support without market backing.

runners_data.name: Samnina
runners_data.comment: A 75,000 euros Sea The Moon filly whose dam was a multiple winner in France over middle distances on soft ground; should handle cut and will likely get further in time. Our figures rank her 10th of 13 and she needs to show her best on debut to get involved.

runners_data.name: Social Circle
runners_data.comment: Wootton Bassett filly out of a high-class 10f Listed-winning dam, so the breeding has real merit for longer trips in time. Jockey bookings suggest she is not the stable's first string here and without any race experience there is little else to weigh beyond pedigree.

races.name: Dubai Duty Free Rockingham Handicap (Premier Handicap)

runners_data.name: Gazelle d'Or
runners_data.note: Strong prominent profile with back-to-back placed efforts at 5f-6f on Good ground at the Curragh; Grassick-Lordan combination is respected, and this horse clearly relishes conditions, making her an ideal stalking candidate.|
runners_data.comment: Progressive filly who was just edged out at Fairyhouse last time, going down by a short-head in an auction race where she may have been slightly outstayed late. Effective at 5-6f on yielding to good; first-time cheekpieces could sharpen the response, though stall 15 and the class step are factors to weigh.

runners_data.name: Toca Madera
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner with 14 of 15 similar-going runs on her card; Tudhope is a key booking for O'Meara and she recorded a 5f Curragh win recently — though the STYLE_FIT flag notes she may be asked to sustain a role under pressure from behind if rivals push.|
runners_data.comment: Back to his very best at Doncaster last time, showing a fine turn of foot from the front to land a handicap by 3½ lengths off a mark 11lb lower; ideally suited by 5f and fast ground. The rise in class and weights are factors, but he rates the clear form pick.

runners_data.name: Likedbymike
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with a consistent placed record at 5f on Good ground for Byrne and Colin Keane — one of the best jockey bookings in the race; needs a truly run race to produce his best from the rear.|
runners_data.comment: Placed in a Listed sprint at Cork last time, beaten just half a length; the strongest form of her career in recent outings and she handles a range of going from heavy to good. A poor overall strike rate is the one concern, but she arrives on the back of a very solid display.

runners_data.name: Erosandpsyche
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up runner who wears a visor and has placed twice at 5f on Good ground in recent starts; at OR=95 the class is there but his 8-year-old profile needs everything to go right late.|
runners_data.comment: Third in a Listed sprint at Cork last time, running to his best after a disappointing spell of form earlier in the season; clearly capable at a high level and acts on any ground. First-time visor here; whether he can translate that Listed effort into a handicap result is the question.

runners_data.name: Stag Night
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent performer who won recently on Soft and placed at 5f Good — the Curragh form is present on softer going but this Good to Firm return is a slight query; W J Lee rides for steady handler McCreery.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a narrow success at this track earlier in the season off a mark 5lb lower, hitting the front by a short-head; ran fifth last time on quicker ground off this same mark and would ideally want some cut. Consistent profile, but the official rating may be stretching him today.

runners_data.name: Eclairage
runners_data.note: A 7-year-old at 5f winner run recently returned a 7th on this going; the 7lb claimer Casey comes in for Murphy's yard which has a quiet recent record and this horse's similar-going figures (0W3P) are workmanlike at best.|
runners_data.comment: Front-running filly with natural pace who overdid it at the head of affairs in a Listed sprint at Cork last time, going down by nine lengths; better suited by today's 5f on a sound surface, and the addition of a first-time tongue-tie may help her race more conservatively.

runners_data.name: Kerdos
runners_data.note: Hold-up type without a win in similar going conditions, returning a string of mid-pack finishes at 5f-6f on Good; apprentice Kearney takes a 3lb claim but the form string shows no victory at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Former Group-level performer whose form has regressed in recent starts, beaten three lengths off a 3lb higher mark at Navan last time; first-time cheekpieces signal that connections are trying something different. The wide draw from stall 17 is an added obstacle, though he retains ability on any ground at 5f.

runners_data.name: Sarahmae
runners_data.note: In-form prominent filly who has won twice in her last six starts including on Good ground; Hogan's yard has been firing with 3 wins from 13 over 14 days and she is lightly weighted coming into this off a quick turnaround.|
runners_data.comment: Thriving in current form, landing a handicap at Down Royal last time by 2¼ lengths off a mark 7lb lower; two recent wins on the board and she handles yielding to good well. Attempting a hat-trick off a career-high mark is a stiff ask, but the momentum is firmly in her favour.

runners_data.name: Dark Ace
runners_data.note: Improving 4-year-old prominent racer who has won twice on Synthetic and placed at 6f on Good; the step back to 5f and switch to genuine Good to Firm at the Curragh is a new test, and 43 days off means fitness requires monitoring.|
runners_data.comment: Hampered and with plenty to make up when closing to be third last time, beaten only a length off 88; the mark here is just 1lb higher. He landed a narrow success at Lingfield on his penultimate outing, and turf on fast ground is the one question today.

runners_data.name: Red Evolution
runners_data.note: Useful prominent type with wins at 5f on Good ground at the Curragh; the 107-day absence is the significant risk factor here — McMonagle takes over in a booking worth noting but the layoff must be respected.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth on his comeback run at Dundalk, beaten 4½ lengths and not at his best returning from a break; his mark has eased in recent starts and he handles a sound surface at 5-6f. Improvement on that reappearance effort looks a fair expectation as fitness levels improve.

runners_data.name: Moltophino
runners_data.note: Carries genuine prominent instincts by nature, though the weight of front-runners in this field means he is likely to find himself racing in midfield rather than his preferred forward pitch — his recent form at 6f on Good is modest.|
runners_data.comment: Double headgear change today — first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces — but Moltophino was too prominent at this track last time, setting it up for rivals and beaten three lengths off a mark just 1lb higher. Generally consistent; hard to fancy against this field on our figures.

runners_data.name: Back Down Under
runners_data.note: Naturally wants to be prominent by inclination but the crowded early stage makes that unlikely; Padraig Roche's runner has hit the frame at 6f on Good but this is a stiffer task over 5f against this class of opposition.|
runners_data.comment: Inconsistent course specialist who moved to the front too soon at this track last time and was beaten two lengths off a mark just 2lb higher; today she wears first-time cheekpieces. She handles good ground at 6-7f, but our figures rank her 16th of 17 and consistency is the concern.

runners_data.name: Cuban Grey
runners_data.note: Likes to race handily and has won at 5f on Standard ground, but the sheer number of rivals with the same agenda will push him back from where he wants to be; recent form at 5f on Good shows a 9th and 7th from his last two.|
runners_data.comment: Won narrowly at Dundalk three starts back off a mark 3lb lower, but showed too much too soon when finishing ninth beaten eight lengths off this same mark last time; inconsistent in recent outings. First-time cheekpieces here and he handles any ground at 5f, but the form is hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Buddy Batt
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner by trade who cannot get that position today given the traffic; Collins' charge has won on Synthetic and Standard but his best similar-going score is limited and he is asked to adapt under Cleary.|
runners_data.comment: Two wins on his recent record and went well through the winter period, but the mark appears to have caught up with him — beaten seven lengths at Dundalk last time off 77. That rating looked stretched on the day and there is little from recent form to suggest a reversal here.

runners_data.name: Shadow Of The Moon
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who won at 5f on Good and placed over 5f on Soft; lightly exposed with a short turnaround, this 4-year-old has an interesting profile but needs a well-run race to bring her finishing kick into play.|
runners_data.comment: Placed on her most recent start at Down Royal, beaten 2¼ lengths off this same mark after stepping down in class; effective over today's trip on soft to good-to-firm ground. A maiden winner now stepping up in handicap grade, she needs a little more to land a blow here.

runners_data.name: Genesis
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer by instinct, pushed to midfield on the map; Mulvany's runner has won at 6f on Good but has struggled to replicate that form recently and the STYLE_FIT tag is a fair caution on his ability to land the scenario he needs.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a half-length success at this track in May off a mark 2lb lower and was a close third on his most recent outing after dropping in class; drops 1lb here. A natural front-runner suited by the trip; first-time cheekpieces add interest, though he is ideally at home on the all-weather.

runners_data.name: Harry's Hill
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up runner, 8 years old, wearing a tongue-tie; Hassett's runner has placed at 5f-6f on Good but the recent form string shows 6th and 12th in similar conditions — needs everything to collapse in his favour late.|
runners_data.comment: Pressed hard up front at Cork last time, doing too much too early and beaten six lengths; form has slipped through recent starts. Stall 16 is a further obstacle, and while first-time tongue-tie is an application for improvement, our figures rank him last of the 17 runners here.

races.paceDynamic: Toca Madera is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 17-horse field on Good to Firm ground at the Curragh over 5f, and with no genuine rival willing to take her on for the lead, she is set to control tempo from the front without being pressured into a suicidal gallop. That said, the pace input behind her is substantial — Gazelle d'Or, Stag Night, Eclairage, Sarahmae, Dark Ace, and Red Evolution are all natural prominent racers who will be pushing for position in the first two furlongs, creating a competitive but not chaotic early dynamic. On Good to Firm ground at the Curragh over a straight 5f, an uncontested lead at a sound but manageable pace strongly favours the front-runner and those tracking closely in the slipstream, as the rail-hugging, prominent-racing profile typically holds an edge when the pace is honest but not extreme. The field contains more genuine prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Moltophino, Back Down Under, Cuban Grey, and Buddy Batt are all natural front-of-the-field operators who are likely to find themselves shuffled into a midfield position they did not choose, with Gazelle d'Or and Toca Madera best placed to actually secure the coveted early spots.

watchPoints.text: Toca Madera — watch whether she gets a clean break from the stalls; if she jumps cleanly and establishes the lead uncontested inside the first furlong, the race is set up to her exact strengths and she becomes very difficult to peg back.

Moltophino, Back Down Under, Cuban Grey, and Buddy Batt — all genuine prominent types who cannot all land their natural position; watch for crowding and possible interference in the first two furlongs as these four fight for berths they cannot all secure.

Red Evolution — the 107-day absence makes fitness a genuine unknown despite the quality jockey booking of McMonagle; if she returns well her 5f Curragh form on Good is strong, but a first-run absence at this level carries real risk.

Sarahmae — watch market moves given Hogan's yard is 3 from 13 over the last 14 days; she is lightly weighted at OR=91, has won twice recently, and a prominent draw combined with a quick turnaround could make her bigger in the race than the OR suggests.

Dark Ace — stepping back in trip from 6f wins on Synthetic to 5f Good to Firm on turf for the first time; if he handles the faster surface and shorter trip the unexposed profile could be interesting, but both questions need answering simultaneously.

races.name: Jebel Ali Racecourse & Stables Dash Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Big Gossey
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old veteran who knows how to race prominently and has two places from three runs on similar Good going at six furlongs; Charles O'Brien has had just one runner in the past fortnight, and 36 days since last run for a horse this age invites a slight freshness query, though his recent placed effort at 6f Good is directly relevant.
runners_data.comment: Back in good form at the Curragh last time, finishing second in a Group 2 contest beaten just 2l having been slightly tardy in making his challenge; a consistent performer at this level who goes particularly well at this venue, first-time tongue-tie applied now, though conceding weight to younger rivals is the ask.

runners_data.name: Bodhi Bear
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 5f Good and is 3W from 5 placed runs on similar going, making him one of the more in-form horses in this field; J A Stack's yard is in decent form (2/8 in 14 days), and stepping up to 6f from a winning 5f run is a standard progression that suits a horse who travels prominently and has the gears to sustain it.
runners_data.comment: Took a handicap at Navan most recently, ¾l to the good on a stiff-tracked course that played to his strengths; effective at 5-6f on good or heavy ground, and with the trainer in form he arrives as a consistent performer with every chance of making an impact in this stronger contest.

runners_data.name: Tango Flare
runners_data.note: Boasts remarkable course-and-distance form — 2 wins and 5 places from 14 runs on similar going — and is the standout hold-up type in terms of raw suitability to the surface; that said, his true style means he needs the field to come back to him in the final furlong, and in a race where Silk Braid may control the pace without being pressured, the gap he faces to bridge could be too large.
runners_data.comment: Showed real determination to prevail by a short-head at Fairyhouse most recently, displaying a willing attitude under pressure; effective at 6f on yielding and good ground, and the new combination of tongue-tie and visor could help reproduce that effort, though he has been inconsistent this season and draws wide in stall 8.

runners_data.name: California Dreamer
runners_data.note: All five recent runs have been over 7f-8f, which raises a genuine distance concern dropping to 6f; going is fine (2/2 placed on similar), but the trip shortening is a significant tactical risk and the yard's high volume (2/18 in 14 days) dilutes the significance of the booking.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 3½l in a Group 2 here last time, reverting around the balance of what she has shown this year after a strong 2025 season; a sound surface suits and that condition is met today, though draw 10 is wide and her recent record reflects a filly below her former best.

runners_data.name: Fregada
runners_data.note: Operates as a genuine hold-up horse but the field's depth of closers means she is unlikely to find her natural berth at the rear, effectively racing out of her preferred position; her recent form figures of 70-966 are uninspiring and her best run on similar going (a win over 5f) came from a more forward position, making this a difficult scenario.
runners_data.comment: Held up at the back in a Listed race at Cork most recently, beaten 3½l without landing a meaningful blow; winless in recent starts and a step back in grade rather than a rise would seem better suited — effective at 6f on a sound surface, but faces a tall order here.

runners_data.name: Little Queenie
runners_data.note: An honest hold-up type at OR 92 who has found the Curragh awkward before (9th at Sandown, mixed STA form) and will struggle to get to the back of a compact ten-runner field; her best efforts have come on Stanmore/flat tracks where hold-up horses can travel more freely, and the fast ground here does not obviously flatter her late-running style.
runners_data.comment: Placed a close third in an auction race at Fairyhouse last time, beaten just ½l in her most recent effort; in decent form over 5-6f on a sound surface, conditions well aligned today, though this step up in class is a tougher ask and another gear forward is required.

runners_data.name: Temperance
runners_data.note: Last ran 353 days ago — by far the longest absence in the field — and drops significantly in class having been rated 80 OR; the hood (p headgear) is a query on a horse returning from nearly a year off, and while she won over 6f Good in her past, the extended layoff makes any form projection highly speculative.
runners_data.comment: Absent for nearly a year and returning here after a tough outing at Group level on her previous start, well beaten; the cheekpieces are new and she usually holds her position until late, which may not suit a quick 6f — significant improvement needed from a mare who hasn't been seen since last summer.

runners_data.name: Oh Cecelia
runners_data.note: A lightly-weighted three-year-old (121lbs) with a genuine hold-up profile and placed efforts at 6f Good, making her the most interesting of the closers in terms of residual upside; K J Condon is a shrewd handler of three-year-olds in Listed company, and Shane Foley's booking adds confidence, though she needs to find a way through from midfield in a race that may be controlled throughout.
runners_data.comment: A progressive filly until her most recent outing at Cork, when she was well beaten without any clear explanation; prior to that she was thriving over 5-6f on a variety of surfaces, and first-time hood applied now as she looks to bounce back from a flat effort.

runners_data.name: Silk Braid
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter and class horse of the race at OR 120, two runs both at 6f Good — a win and a second — giving her a perfect profile for this shape; Colin Keane for G M Lyons is a potent booking, though having raced just twice she carries a small element of unexposed uncertainty, and the [STYLE_FIT] tag is a mild caution given she maps as Prominent rather than a pure lead horse.
runners_data.comment: Stepped up sharply in class on her seasonal reappearance, going down by just 1¼l in a Listed contest at Navan — a striking effort for a lightly-raced filly; fast ground will suit her action and she handles the trip, though draw 9 is wide and limited form makes hard assessment difficult.

runners_data.name: Tahcawin
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who handles 6f Good well (placed twice, won once) and will race prominently enough to be competitive if Silk Braid does not fully get away with the race; Gary Carroll is a good fit for a horse who needs to be ridden with tactical aggression, and the 42-day gap is not a concern given the form is recent enough.
runners_data.comment: Progressive filly who finished strongly to be a close third in a Group 3 at Naas last time, the run hinting that 7f would suit even better; effective on good ground and with cut in it, she handles these conditions and arrives as our top-rated runner with a combination of form and upside.

races.paceDynamic: Silk Braid is the confirmed front-runner here, and with Colin Keane in the saddle for G M Lyons, she is likely to stride into a clear lead from the outset on Good to Firm ground over 6f at the Curragh. She faces no genuine front-running challenger in this field, meaning the pace she sets will be self-managed and sustainable rather than pressured — a controlled gallop that could play directly into her hands if she has enough class over these rivals. Big Gossey, Bodhi Bear, and Tahcawin will push forward from the prominent berths, applying some cover pressure but unlikely to match Silk Braid stride-for-stride early. This race shape — a single front-runner with a clear, uncontested lead on fast ground — heavily favours the leader and prominent horses who can travel close to the pace, as genuine hold-up types face a near-impossible task if the early tempo is not scorching. Note that the field holds more hold-up types than can realistically race from the rear: Fregada, Little Queenie, and Temperance are true hold-up horses who are mapped to midfield precisely because they cannot all get to the back of this field, meaning they will race out of their preferred role and their effectiveness in any late-closing shape is materially reduced.

watchPoints.text: Silk Braid jumping cleanly — if Colin Keane gets her out smartly from whatever draw she has, the race could be over as a contest by the two-furlong pole; any stumble or crowding at the start is the main single danger to the favourite's chance.

Temperance's return after 353 days off is a significant unknown — she carries the shortest race-fitness profile in the field by a wide margin, and if she shows any signs of over-freshness or greenness early, she could cause interference to horses around her in a ten-runner sprint.

The three redistributed hold-up horses (Fregada, Little Queenie, Temperance) will all be competing for midfield positions they do not naturally want — watch for crowding or checking on the inside rail in the first two furlongs as they fail to find their preferred spots.

California Dreamer's fitness for 6f is worth monitoring in the betting markets — if she drifts significantly pre-race it would confirm punter concern about the trip drop, which would be a useful signal about market confidence in a horse who is technically capable on the going.

Bodhi Bear's draw and early position are worth noting at the off — if he can slot into second or third place behind Silk Braid without being shuffled back, his recent winning form and strong record on similar going make him the most likely beneficiary if the favourite is caught near the line.

races.name: Dubai Duty Free Derby Festival Handicap (Premier Handicap)

runners_data.name: Lord Massusus
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Joseph Murphy ridden by apprentice Paddy Harnett; 49 days off the track is worth noting, and while his best form on similar going is moderate (one win from 15 similar-going starts), he needs a truly run race to land a blow from the back of this field.
runners_data.comment: Suited by today's trip and ground, Lord Massusus was too keen when well beaten in a Listed contest last time but could respond positively in this lesser grade; he has been out of form in recent starts and his mark looks stiff, though earlier evidence suggests he can be competitive when settling properly.

runners_data.name: Perry Mason
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner tagged with a style-fit flag, meaning his best form has often come over longer trips where he can use his stamina; the drop back to a flat mile at Curragh is the key question, but his uncontested lead is a significant tactical asset and T14 shows the yard in decent nick (1/8).
runners_data.comment: Won here by a nose two starts back before flattening out badly over a longer trip last time, Perry Mason drops back to a more suitable distance today; from a wide draw carrying the same high mark, he will need things to fall right to get competitive.

runners_data.name: Far From Dandy
runners_data.note: Stephen Thorne's four-year-old has back-to-back placed efforts at this exact trip and going band, carries a hood, and sits just 42 days off his last run; a genuine prominent type who should get his position early and is one of the more straightforward pace-map fits in the race.
runners_data.comment: Placed in his last two outings and unfortunate at Naas last time when meeting trouble after being held up, Far From Dandy arrives relatively fresh and tries first-time cheekpieces at a venue he handles; effective at today's trip and on a mark just a pound higher than last time.

runners_data.name: State Actor
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride on this six-year-old returning from a lengthy 238-day absence for W T Farrell; has placed form at this track and distance on good ground but the layoff is a significant flag, and jumping straight back into a competitive Premier Handicap demands immediate fitness.
runners_data.comment: Absent for almost eight months and expected to benefit from this run, State Actor trailed home well down the field here on his last start but remains effective at today's trip on any ground; a mark with scope could make him competitive once he regains full fitness.

runners_data.name: Orandi
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old carrying a tongue-tie who has been out of the frame in all five recent starts, including twice finishing seventh or worse at this trip on good ground; the age and form string make it hard to make a case, even if A J Martin's charge was once more competitive.
runners_data.comment: Beaten three and a half lengths off a higher mark at Limerick last time, Orandi is back for the first time in over two months wearing a first-time tongue-tie; best around today's trip but from a wide draw with a patchy recent record, he is difficult to trust for a bold showing.

runners_data.name: Zarathos
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle teams up with in-form trainer Dylan Cunha (4/24 in 14 days) on a four-year-old who has won twice over seven furlongs and once over this mile trip on good ground; arguably the best recent form profile in the field and a natural prominent runner well-placed in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Won back-to-back before going close last time beaten a neck off a lower mark, Zarathos is in excellent form and ideally suited by fast ground here; operating off a 5lb higher mark now but continuing to progress, he is very much the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Coeur d'Or
runners_data.note: Dermot Weld's ten-year-old is a front-runner by inclination but cannot get that position in this overloaded field — his recent form has largely come over longer trips, and the style-fit discount applies here, so treat his chance with caution despite Weld's customary precision in placing horses.
runners_data.comment: Back in form with consecutive placings, Coeur d'Or showed real determination at Leopardstown last time when beaten just a length and a half; proven at this course and distance on suitable going, he arrives with tongue-tie and blinkers for the first time and holds strong claims.

runners_data.name: Slieve Binnian
runners_data.note: A natural pace horse for David Marnane who won twice over seven furlongs on good ground but has been out of the frame in six consecutive runs, most recently at longer distances; pushed back into midfield by the crowded prominent group and his current form gives little confidence he can compensate by finishing through.
runners_data.comment: Successful in this race last year and effective on quick ground like today, Slieve Binnian was comfortably held at Leopardstown last time and needs to show considerably more; ranked at the foot of our figures, he requires a significant bounce-back to feature.

runners_data.name: Booyea
runners_data.note: Thomas Gibney's six-year-old is a genuine hold-up performer with two wins from 15 similar-going starts, wears a hood, and was beaten only five lengths in his most recent run; W J Lee in the saddle adds interest and he is one of the more credible closers if the pace does develop late.
runners_data.comment: Drawn wide again from stall 11 and on a run of poor form, Booyea was caught wide at Leopardstown last time on what may have been unsuitable ground; first-time blinkers could help on a more amenable surface, but he needs to reverse a declining trend to get involved.

runners_data.name: Playin Cool
runners_data.note: Ronan Whelan partners this four-year-old who is a confirmed prominent racer but cannot hold that slot in this field — his best placing on similar going is limited (one placed from six runs) and his form trail mixes stamina trips with shorter; the redistribution materially dents his prospects.
runners_data.comment: Back to his best at Leopardstown last time when edged out narrowly late off a lower mark, Playin Cool is on a fair mark and effective at the trip; today's quicker ground is the main query, having shown his best form with more cut underfoot.

runners_data.name: Pierre Royal
runners_data.note: Has winning and placed form at this exact trip on good ground for Adrian McGuinness, a trainer who has been firing (2/28 in 14 days), and Adam Caffrey takes the ride; a natural front-runner pushed into a midfield slot by the crowded map, so his ability to recapture a forward position early will be decisive.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Limerick last time when failing to land a blow, Pierre Royal remains on a mark worth another look given his breeding; effective at today's trip on suitable ground and lightly raced enough to improve on that effort.

runners_data.name: Pretty Omagh Girl
runners_data.note: Ben Coen's mount won over this exact trip on good ground most recently for A Oliver, who has been active and placed (2/21); she is a natural prominent racer remapped to midfield by the field's density, but her recent course-and-distance win is hard to ignore if Coen can work her forward cleanly in the early stages.
runners_data.comment: Landed her handicap debut here by four lengths with something to spare last time, Pretty Omagh Girl looks capable of absorbing the 10lb rise with more progress to come; effective at today's trip and continuing to improve, she is a serious danger.

runners_data.name: Red Charlie
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery trains and rides his own horse, which is a notable angle in a competitive Premier Handicap; the four-year-old wears a tongue-tie and showed placed form over shorter on soft, but his good-ground figures at a mile are thin (no wins or places over this trip/going) and he is best treated as an each-way outsider.
runners_data.comment: Won here comfortably three starts back and unlucky at his penultimate start, Red Charlie performed to expectation last time when stepped up in trip; a first-time tongue-tie from a wide draw, he is ideally suited by a sharper test at 7f but handles the mile and remains of interest.

races.paceDynamic: Perry Mason is the lone confirmed front-runner and, on Good To Firm ground over a flat Curragh mile, is expected to set a controlled, sustainable gallop without meaningful pressure from a genuine pace rival. The field, however, is saturated with prominent-style horses — Slieve Binnian, Coeur d'Or, Playin Cool, Pierre Royal and Pretty Omagh Girl are all natural prominent racers who cannot all occupy their preferred position, meaning several will be forced to race in unfamiliar midfield slots and their effectiveness will be compromised. Perry Mason's uncontested lead at a sensible tempo creates a race that plays squarely into the hands of prominent horses who do secure an early position — specifically Far From Dandy, Zarathos and State Actor — rather than the shuffled-back true hold-up types. The tactical verdict is clear: in a steady, front-runner-controlled mile on fast ground with a packed prominent group behind, horses who travel close to the pace without being caught in traffic — genuine prominent runners who get their position — are the profile to follow, while true hold-up runners must produce their best from the back of a potentially strung-out field.

watchPoints.text: Perry Mason's early sectionals will set the tone for the entire race — if Leigh Roche is allowed to bowl along uncontested at a true pace, the front-runner/prominent profile dominates; watch whether Far From Dandy or Zarathos attempt to press him and alter the tempo.

The cluster of displaced prominent horses — Slieve Binnian, Coeur d'Or, Playin Cool, Pierre Royal and Pretty Omagh Girl — all trying to work forward from mapped midfield positions creates a serious crowding risk turning into the straight; any interference here could produce dramatic position changes.

State Actor's 238-day absence is the longest layoff in the field by a wide margin; Colin Keane is a world-class pilot but even he cannot fully compensate for a horse returning cold into a Premier Handicap, and a slow start or lack of fitness at the two-furlong pole should be flagged early.

Pretty Omagh Girl's most recent win came over this exact course, distance and going band — if Ben Coen slots her handy in the first few furlongs rather than accepting a midfield berth, her form profile makes her a live threat that the market may not fully respect.

races.name: Dubai Duty Free International Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Crown Of Oaks
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 4yo with two wins at this sort of trip, returning from 253 days off for Haggas — freshness can cut both ways, and although her natural inclination is to race close to the pace, the crowded prominent berths in this field mean she is unlikely to get the position she wants, which is a meaningful concern on return from such a long layoff.
runners_data.comment: A handicapper on the upgrade last season, winning at Ascot to show he handles 8-10f well in any conditions; returning after eight months on the sidelines, this is a tough test on his comeback against top-level rivals, though the trainer is in form and improvement looks likely once race-fit.

runners_data.name: Hotazhell
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners this 4yo who has been consistent without winning lately, running in headgear that suggests connections are trying to sharpen her up; nine runs on similar going from twelve starts shows she handles these conditions, but her trip form is mixed and she'll need to find a length or two on recent efforts.
runners_data.comment: Just headed in the final strides at Navan last time, ¼l third in a Listed contest after being in a winning position close home — a strong effort; first-time cheekpieces for a horse who has landed at the top level in the past and is effective at 8-10f; that prior class makes him a serious rival here.

runners_data.name: Purview
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner and a horse in excellent form with back-to-back wins on Good and Good to Firm, Keane can take him to the front unchallenged and control the pace entirely — his style fit is ideal for the shape he creates, making him the central figure around whom the entire race pivots.
runners_data.comment: Moving through the race with ease before finding an extra gear to take a Listed contest here by six lengths last time, a dominant display that suggested he has genuinely stepped forward; effective at 10-12f on a sound surface and the step up in grade looks well within his compass.

runners_data.name: Tiberius Thunder
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse who has been consistent without troubling the judge, his best figures have come in slower-ground races and his record on Good to Firm does not inspire — the 16-day turnaround is fine physically but there is no compelling reason to believe this race shape will suddenly unlock him.
runners_data.comment: Wore blinkers most recently at Gowran Park and raced far too freely, a pattern that contributed to a 7½l third and confirmed the tendency to run below his best this season; effective at 8-10f and today's fast ground suits his action, but winless in recent starts and with much to establish here.

runners_data.name: Trustyourinstinct
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good at his most recent start for Joseph O'Brien and is proven across a range of ground; the J M Sheridan booking is notable and this 6yo's record of five wins from fifteen similar-going starts shows he thrives in conditions like today, making him one of the most interesting prominent-to-midfield types in the field.
runners_data.comment: Dropped down to a Conditions race at Gowran Park last time and produced his best effort of the season, asserting by 1½l against lesser opposition; landed this contest last year and has a strong overall record at the Curragh, effective at 10-12f on any ground — back in form and drawn low in stall 1.

runners_data.name: Sindria
runners_data.note: A 4yo with a win over 10f on Good who is better suited to travelling prominently, but with several others aiming for the same early positions, she is likely to end up in a more restrained role than suits her — Dylan Browne McMonagle's strong judgement may soften that blow, but the style mismatch is real.
runners_data.comment: Third in a Listed race at Navan last time, performing creditably under a big weight just a length off the winner; continuing to develop and the return to 10f — a distance that suits her better than a mile — looks well-timed, with her stable carrying a good record in this contest.

runners_data.name: Geryon
runners_data.note: Consistent placed horse for G M Lyons who has run well at shorter trips on similar going; the tongue-tie is already a known factor, but this 3yo is another natural prominent type likely to find himself shuffled back in the early stages, and racing out of role over a trip that may already be stretching him limits his prospects.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a neck in a Listed contest at Navan last time, producing an encouraging effort as he stepped up in trip; has been gradually progressing throughout the season and the first-time tongue-tie could help further, though yet to score in recent starts and this is a step up again in grade.

runners_data.name: Isaac Newton
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride for A P O'Brien on this lightly raced 3yo who won over 9f on Good last time; a genuine prominent racer by inclination, he will struggle to get close to the front with Purview dominating that space, and his form at longer trips is unproven — Moore's positional intelligence is the best asset here.
runners_data.comment: Got home by a neck in a Listed contest at Navan last time, digging deep after meeting trouble in running — a gutsy effort; stays 10f, handles today's conditions, and with an elite booking pairing and the stable's strong record in this contest, heads our figures as the one to beat.

races.paceDynamic: Purview is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Colin Keane can dictate a controlled, sustainable tempo on Good to Firm ground over 1m2f at the Curragh — a track that rewards horses able to conserve energy before the final rise. The pace will be honest but not brutal, set by a horse who has proven he can both lead and quicken, which is a dangerous combination when unopposed. This field holds more prominent-minded types than can physically occupy those early positions: Crown Of Oaks, Sindria, Geryon, and Isaac Newton are all natural prominent racers who are mapped to midfield purely because the space in front is taken, meaning the race shape is unlikely to be genuinely cut up by them. The controlled lead suits a horse with tactical speed and a strong finishing kick — classically advantaging the horse who can travel in the slipstream of an uncontested front-runner and produce a powerful sustained finish, meaning prominent-to-midfield closers with a strong RPR and proven finishing ability on similar going are best placed.

Crown Of Oaks has been off the track for 253 days; watch the market in the final hour for any signs of stable confidence, as a fresh, well-handicapped Haggas runner returning to form at this trip would be a significant threat if ready to run to her best.

The redistribution of Isaac Newton, Geryon, Crown Of Oaks and Sindria into midfield positions means the early-race tactical picture could be congested and rougher than a straightforward lead-and-kick scenario — watch how quickly Moore, McMonagle and Carroll settle their mounts in the first two furlongs.

races.name: Dubai Duty Free Celebration Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Alcantor
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner for O'Brien and McMonagle who will set the pace here, but similar-going form reads poorly (0 wins, 0 places from 15 similar-ground runs) and a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.91 suggests its rating reflects a different position — monitor whether it can sustain the lead under pressure.|
runners_data.comment: Twice successful at Group level in France with high-class form to his name; he found 7f too sharp last time, beaten 7½ lengths in a Group 3 at Epsom, but today's mile is a much better fit. He could prove significantly superior to these rivals if he recaptures his French form.

runners_data.name: Cowardofthecounty
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 7f on Good and has solid similar-going credentials (2W2P from 12 runs), making this a legitimate hold-up candidate for O'Brien whose chance hinges entirely on whether the pace is strong enough to suit a genuine closer over this trip.|
runners_data.comment: Won a conditions race at Fairyhouse last time by two lengths, benefitting from a strong pace; a Group winner at two and by no means a token stable runner. He is effective at 7-8f with cut in the ground, though today's quick surface may not play to his strengths.

runners_data.name: Tokenomics
runners_data.note: David Marnane's five-year-old is a natural prominent racer with a strong record at this trip (3W5P from 15 similar-ground runs including a recent second on Good), and tracking Alcantor from a forward position on fast ground looks an ideal setup.|
runners_data.comment: Second in a Listed contest at Leopardstown last time, beaten just 1¼ lengths; progressive on his profile and versatile over 7-9f on any going. Stepping into this grade from handicaps brings some uncertainty, but he has proved himself capable at Listed level and is genuinely unexposed here.

runners_data.name: Zodiac Bear
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners this J P Murtagh-trained four-year-old who won over 7f on Good last time and has prominent-racing credentials; stepping up to a mile on similar ground is the key query but the course form is encouraging.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth in a conditions race at Leopardstown on his return from a layoff, having found himself with plenty to make up late; a promising sort expected to come on considerably for that run. The stable has a strong record in this contest and he is effective at 7f on soft to good ground.

runners_data.name: Duckadilly
runners_data.note: Trainer McLoughlin without a winner in 14 days, and though Duckadilly won over this course and distance on Good, it is a genuine prominent racer that the pace map has pushed into a midfield role because Alcantor has first claim on the front — whether it can still get a forward position from its draw is the critical question.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a Listed race at Navan last time by half a length, dropping in grade to get there; handles 7-8f on yielding to good and is generally consistent. The opposition at Navan was modest for the grade, so she needs to step forward here to trouble the principals.

runners_data.name: Spicy Margarita
runners_data.note: Robson De Aguiar's hold-up filly returns after 86 days off, has been running at longer trips (10f-12f) recently, and the step back down to a mile on quick ground for a true hold-up type relying on a pace scenario that may not materialise makes her an outsider with multiple questions to answer.|
runners_data.comment: Struggling on deep ground when well beaten in a Group 3 at this track last time; better suited by a sounder surface and returning from a short break. Effective at 8-10f on good ground, she needs to recapture earlier form and a response is required after that disappointing display.

runners_data.name: Accredited
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore rides for A P O'Brien and this three-year-old, a natural prominent racer by profile, has been placed into a midfield map position through redistribution — Moore's positional intelligence could help it reclaim a forward berth, but at OR 93 stepping into Listed company off just three career runs it faces a stiff class test.|
runners_data.comment: Well below his prior level when beaten seven lengths in a 3yo race at Naas last time, never in contention; fitted with first-time blinkers today and has strong connections who may get more from him. Better form beforehand suggests scope for improvement over today's trip, and he will stay further in time.

races.paceDynamic: Alcantor is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a seven-runner field, is set to control proceedings from the front at a sustainable, uncontested tempo on Good to Firm ground at The Curragh. Tokenomics and Zodiac Bear are the natural prominent challengers who will look to track Alcantor through the early and middle stages, while Cowardofthecounty and Spicy Margarita are the legitimate hold-up horses who will be covered up and rely on a strong late surge. This field contains more prominent types than the map can accommodate — Duckadilly and Accredited are both true front-runners or prominent racers by nature but have been redistributed to midfield given Alcantor's dominance and the congestion near the front; Alcantor and Tokenomics are most likely to actually secure those forward positions. The uncontested, controlled pace on fast ground strongly favours horses that can race close to the pace and sustain their effort through the final furlong, giving a clear edge to prominent-position horses who travel well and quicken — pure hold-up tactics are a harder ask when the pace is not truly searching.

races.name: Dubai Duty Free Irish Derby (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Action
runners_data.note: Progressive A P O'Brien three-year-old with placed efforts at Listed/Group level at a mile and 10f on Good ground; a natural prominent racer whose position in the mid-pack on this map reflects the overcrowded early positions rather than his instinct, and the style fit penalty should temper expectations if he cannot get forward.|
runners_data.comment: High-class colt whose trainer's yard has a strong record in this race, Action was sent forward too prominently and failed to stay in testing conditions at Epsom in a Group 1 last time; better ground here and a more restrained ride could see him show his true quality at today's trip.

runners_data.name: Benvenuto Cellini
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partnership with A P O'Brien, four wins from six starts including two at a mile on Good ground and a 12f run at Softs; sits comfortably in a tracking role and the step to 1m4f on fast ground looks well within range given his pedigree and middle-distance form.|
runners_data.comment: Won a Group 3 at Chester by four lengths last time with authority, Benvenuto Cellini was a non-runner at Epsom due to a stalls incident before that and that run should be set aside; proven at 12f with the faster surface strongly in his favour and a top stable behind him, he is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Bunyola Bay
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon runner who has won twice on Good going at 7f and 10f with Sean Levey, including a recent Goodwood win; his three-race form is short but sharp, he handles Good ground well, and while the field will crowd his preferred position the step up to 1m4f is the unknown factor.|
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins including a three-length success at Gowran Park last time, Bunyola Bay is bred to get further and should benefit from the step up to 12f; he steps up markedly in class here, however, and faces a considerably stronger test than he has encountered so far.

runners_data.name: Christmas Day
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter for this race, with four wins and consistent front-running across 8f to 12f on various grounds including a 12f Softs win; Ronan Whelan knows his horse's gears and an uncontested lead on Good to Firm could be decisive if he has the class to sustain it at Group 1 level.|
runners_data.comment: Winner of the Group 1 at Epsom by three lengths last time, Christmas Day showed real quality at this trip and acts on any going; the faster surface today may not play to his strengths and the bare form is hard to weigh up, but he is unquestionably a major contender.

runners_data.name: James J Braddock
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle rides the Joseph O'Brien-trained gelding who won at 10f on Good but has struggled when stepping up to 12f in softer conditions (3rd at Softs); the redistribution reflects his inability to get his natural forward spot, and his 12f stamina on quick ground remains unproven.|
runners_data.comment: Five and a quarter lengths third in a Group 1 at Epsom last time, James J Braddock proved he handles this trip and remains progressive; this course is expected to suit him and there looks to be further improvement to come.

runners_data.name: Pierre Bonnard
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien runner with two wins over 10f on Good and Heathon ground but back-to-back 7ths at 12f on Softs suggest the trip in softer conditions is demanding; mapped to hold-up from a natural prominent style purely by field arithmetic, and that positional shift combined with his unimpressive 12f form makes this a difficult assignment.|
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in a Group 1 at Epsom last time and yet to fulfil his potential consistently, Pierre Bonnard has the backing of a trainer who knows this race well; he stays the trip and acts on any going, and remains capable of better on his day.

runners_data.name: Raaheeb
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows' unbeaten two-from-two runner (10f Good, 7f Soft) arrives fresh on 65 days since last run, which is the main unknown; Rossa Ryan takes over and the horse clearly has ability, but stepping straight to a Group 1 Irish Derby over 1m4f from a small sample of form is a big ask regardless of how well he has won.|
runners_data.comment: Won back-to-back with a smooth three-length Group 3 victory at Sandown last time, Raaheeb arrives with an unbeaten record but has been off for 65 days; he is expected to get this trip and is likely to keep progressing, though the fast ground combined with his absence is a concern.

runners_data.name: Shaihaan
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien-trained runner for Tom Marquand who found a win over 10f on Heathon ground but has no better than third in his last three and his trainer is 0/20 in the past 14 days; shows as midfield due to the packed prominent group, which mirrors what is likely to happen in running, and his 1m4f form on Good ground is limited.|
runners_data.comment: Third in a Group 3 here last time, running his race without quite reaching the front rank, Shaihaan sits at the foot of our figures in this company; effective at 8-10f on a variety of going, he may need the principals to underperform to feature.

races.paceDynamic: Christmas Day is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no other horse likely to seriously dispute early, Ronan Whelan can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over 1m4f at the Curragh. The pace will be genuine but measured — Christmas Day's record shows a consistent leader who does not capitulate, meaning this is not a dawdle but nor is it a war, and that creates a relatively compressed race shape through the first mile. Horses like James J Braddock, Action, Shaihaan and Bunyola Bay are all natural prominent types in form but cannot all occupy those berths simultaneously; in practice, Christmas Day gets the rail and the lead, while the remaining prominent types jostle for position just behind, burning more energy than they would ideally spend. This race shape — a controlled solo lead on fast ground at a classic trip — most strongly favours a horse with tactical versatility that can sit just off the pace, has proven stamina for 1m4f, and can produce a sustained run rather than a pure sprint finish; Benvenuto Cellini and Raaheeb fit that profile best, while the redistribution of multiple prominent types into the mid-pack slightly compromises their individual chances in slower-run scenario shapes. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all get their natural position; Christmas Day is virtually certain to lead, Benvenuto Cellini and Raaheeb are best placed to sit second and third, while Action, James J Braddock, Shaihaan and Bunyola Bay will be shuffled wider and further back than their trainers would choose.

watchPoints.text: Christmas Day — watch whether Ronan Whelan is able to slot onto the rail uncontested in the first furlong; if another runner challenges him for the lead before the first bend, the pace will lift sharply and alter the entire race shape.

James J Braddock, Action and Shaihaan — all natural front-runners forced back; monitor the early jostling between stalls 3 and 8 for potential crowding, bumping or a wide run that costs ground and energy before the race settles.

Raaheeb — 65 days off the track is the single biggest unknown; watch his behaviour in the paddock and his early race demeanour for any sign of ring-rustiness before drawing conclusions about his chances.

Benvenuto Cellini — Ryan Moore is likely to use his positional experience to slot into second or third on the inner early; if he is blocked or forced wide in the first half-mile by the prominent-type congestion, his race becomes significantly harder to win.

Pierre Bonnard — his back-to-back 7th-place finishes at 12f on Softs are a form concern at this trip regardless of pace shape; watch whether Wayne Lordan rides him conservatively from the outset, suggesting the team are managing expectations rather than expecting a big run.

races.name: Tulfarris Hotel And Golf Resort Maddenstown Handicap (Premier Handicap)

runners_data.name: Listentodwindblow
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for O'Brien, won over 1m last time out on Good ground 4 days ago; tongue tie fitted, strong sim-going record of 4/7 suggests the trip and conditions are fine, but fighting for the lead against two rivals makes it hard to dominate.
runners_data.comment: Broke through in a maiden at Naas most recently, benefiting from a positive front-running ride on a reduced trip; returning just four days later with a first-time tongue-tie, effective at 7-10f with some give underfoot, though stepping up in distance here and the official rating does ask more on handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Satoyama
runners_data.note: Prominent-running O'Brien second string with Dylan Browne McMonagle, won over 1m on Good ground 28 days ago; only three runs visible but two on similar going were both placed or won, and stepping up to 1m1f should suit a horse who stays well.
runners_data.comment: Form from his maiden win has been boosted by subsequent events, and he held his level well at Listowel last time, filling fourth just 1¼l off the pace in a Conditions race; effective at 7-8f on soft or yielding ground, though draw 13 and an official mark that asks for more are the checks.

runners_data.name: Bobby McGee
runners_data.note: In exceptional form with three wins from his last three, all at 1m on Good ground, and Chris Hayes keeps the ride; the step to 1m1f looks well within range for a horse whose sim-going record is 6/7, and he arrives as the most in-form runner in the field.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in recent starts, including a 3yo race at Naas last time when a stiff track played to his strengths; yet to be fully tested at this trip and appears to hold strong potential at this level, though draw 17 and six weeks since his last run are factors.

runners_data.name: Summer Is Tomorrow
runners_data.note: O'Brien third string, prominent runner who wants cut in the ground (visor fitted) and a recent poor run on Good to Firm last time over 9f raises a going concern; form figures on similar ground are modest at 7/9, so the conditions here are a question mark.
runners_data.comment: Juvenile form was notably strong, and this return to handicap company after being well beaten in a Listed contest at Navan last time looks a better opportunity; bred and apparently built for 10f, acts on soft and good, and the first-time visor adds another dimension on his handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Antigua
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride for A P O'Brien, blinkers and tongue tie fitted; won over 1m2f on Good last time, steps back in trip, and his front-running style puts him in the middle of the early battle — he has the class to possibly survive it but has to prove he handles being pressed from the off.
runners_data.comment: Took a maiden at Fairyhouse by 3¼l last time, the first-time headgear combination clearly unlocking an upturn in form when ridden positively; effective at 10-12f on yielding and good, and a debut handicap mark that gives him room to manoeuvre for a still-progressive sort with a leading jockey-trainer partnership in place makes him a compelling threat.

runners_data.name: Brownstown
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Gavin Cromwell who has shown his best form when covering ground late; placed twice on Good ground in recent history, but sim-going record of 5/7 without a win suggests he needs things to go right for him at the business end.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in recent starts and well below her best at Gowran Park last time, going down the field over a longer trip; form has been inconsistent and the trainer is out of sorts, though her sire brings stamina and the first-time tongue-tie is worth a note.

runners_data.name: How'sthebai
runners_data.note: Colin Keane partnership for Lyons, front-runner who has won on soft and standard but sim-going record on Good is 1/5 with no wins — that is a genuine flag on this surface, and being embroiled in a three-way pace battle compounds the concern.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in his last five starts, the most recent a handicap at Leopardstown going up in trip on a softer surface; the form has since been validated, but a sharp hike to the official rating makes this a much stiffer test, and our figures rank him towards the foot of the 18-runner field.

runners_data.name: Rolltight
runners_data.note: Ben Coen on a horse with a spotless Good-ground profile — all three career runs on similar going, two wins and a second; prominent-running type stepping up in trip and handicap company for the first time after a 39-day break, but the form is strong and the conditions suit.
runners_data.comment: Made his mark at Gowran Park on his most recent start, winning his maiden by ¾l over a mile on good to yielding; from an in-form stable, his form has held up well since and the mark looks reasonable for a progressive sort, the main note being draw 18.

runners_data.name: Manton Bay
runners_data.note: Prominent stayer who was second over 1m2f last time on Good, suggesting the extra furlong of today's trip is a plus; 43 days since last run and modest sim-going record of 2/4, but Luke McAteer can ride him patiently off the hot pace.
runners_data.comment: Went close on handicap debut at Navan last time, beaten by just half a length off a 4lb lower mark while moving smoothly through the race; bred for middle distances and 9f should suit, though 43 days since his last run and draw 5 both ask for a clean passage.

runners_data.name: King Of Earth
runners_data.note: William Haggas-trained visitor ridden by Tom Marquand, wears a hood; won last time at 1m on Standard and sim-going record on Good is 1/4, so the surface is unproven — prominent style means he will be shuffled around in the early stages.
runners_data.comment: A Kingman-bred colt who made no mistake at Wolverhampton on his latest start, dropping in class to edge a narrow win; form since has been endorsed and a debut handicap mark that appears to give him scope gives him solid prospects here, with first-time cheekpieces adding a potential extra gear on a sound surface.

runners_data.name: Stars Will Shine
runners_data.note: Adam Caffrey takes over for Noel Meade; won on Good ground over 7f and has shown ability, but a poor run last time (9th) and stepping up in trip and class simultaneously makes this a tough ask, even if the ground is fine.
runners_data.comment: Off the back of a below-par handicap debut here, where she was beaten 7¼l over this trip, there are stamina questions to answer at 9f; suited by 6-7f and preferring cut underfoot, the conditions are not ideally aligned and she faces a significant challenge stepping back up.

runners_data.name: Monvoe
runners_data.note: Three wins from last five runs and strong form on Good ground; a naturally prominent racer whose position in this analysis is shown as hold-up solely because the field is overloaded with prominent types — his actual racing style is forward and his form figures are excellent, but he will need to navigate traffic if pushed further back than ideal.
runners_data.comment: In fine form across recent starts, landing a handicap at Limerick last time by half a length having needed to call on all his reserves over 7-8f; could produce another solid run, though our figures rank him 13 of 18 here and the step up in class is a notable ask.

runners_data.name: Cherry Hill Girl
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for Slattery whose best efforts on Good ground were a pair of thirds over longer trips; decent stamina profile for 1m1f and the late-run style suits a strong pace, though sim-going record of 3/8 without a win flags that wins have proved elusive.
runners_data.comment: Plugged into third at Gowran Park last time, finishing 6¼l off the winner in a 3yo race; consistent in nature but yet to score in recent starts, and this step up in class makes it a significant ask — effective at 7-8f with cut, she is outpaced on our figures.

runners_data.name: Sanctijude
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan rides a horse who is naturally a prominent racer — won over 1m on Good last time — but the field's density of pace means he is unlikely to get that position and will be shuffled back to midfield against his instincts; McCreery trainer record of 0/16 over 14 days is also uninspiring.
runners_data.comment: Winning at Gowran Park last time by a short-head — her best effort in recent starts — Sanctijude now tries first-time cheekpieces; effective at 7-8f on a range of going and consistent at her level, though making a clear step up in grade today means more will be required.

runners_data.name: Anushka
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead runner who wants to race prominently and has placed twice on Good ground, but in a field this pacy she will almost certainly race further back than suits her; the Going is fine, the trip is a slight question, and Andrew Slattery is the trainer's jockey.
runners_data.comment: Finished strongly to be beaten 2l here last time, performing to her mark off a 1lb higher mark at up to a mile; for a leading Irish stable with this trip and track within her comfort zone, building on that effort looks possible — a late-running style could suit if the pace is genuine.

runners_data.name: Punica Granatum
runners_data.note: Shane Foley on a Harrington-trained filly with two seconds on Good ground and a decent recent form line; she is a front-foot runner who will be squeezed out of her natural position by the confirmed pace horses, and racing from further back than usual adds difficulty rather than helping.
runners_data.comment: Going down by a short-head on handicap debut here last time, returning from a break at a 3lb lower mark — an encouraging effort for a consistent filly over this trip on good ground; yet to score in recent starts but has placed steadily, and another solid run is within reach.

runners_data.name: Liberation Date
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago which is a serious freshness concern; a naturally prominent racer who, beyond the redistribution point, arrives here on a poor recent run sequence of 9-6-8 and will face a stiff task racing out of her preferred position on fast ground.
runners_data.comment: Beaten 5¼l in a handicap here just two days ago and ranked last of the 18 on our figures; stamina is a concern as she steps up in trip, best at 7f, and the combination of a quick turnaround and longer distance makes a compelling case difficult to construct.

runners_data.name: Ryefield Dasher
runners_data.note: Thomas Gibney-trained runner with a modest form record — best effort a 4th on Good over 8f — and sim-going record of 1/4; a prominent-running type who won't get that role today, and the overall profile makes it hard to identify a winning scenario for this horse.
runners_data.comment: Racing too keenly at Leopardstown last time, he emptied quickly and was well held; winless in recent starts and the tendency to overrace over this sort of trip makes it hard to see a reversal here, leaving him vulnerable in a competitive field.

races.paceDynamic: Listentodwindblow, How'sthebai and Antigua are all confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the off on Good to Firm ground over 1m1f at the Curragh, virtually guaranteeing a strong, sustained gallop from the outset. With three horses fighting for the front, the pace will be genuine throughout, stretching the field and testing stamina as they turn for home, leaving little room for a tactical dawdle. The field also contains a significant surplus of prominent-running types — Sanctijude, Anushka, Punica Granatum, Liberation Date and Ryefield Dasher are all natural prominent racers who cannot all secure their preferred position and will be shuffled back into midfield, meaning the true pace picture is even more compressed at the front than the map suggests. This race shape strongly favours hold-up or late-finishing profiles who can travel comfortably off the strong pace and produce a sustained run from off the heels of the leaders in the final two furlongs, with genuine front-runners who can handle pressure and prominent horses with stamina reserves also in the mix.
