watchPoints.text: Bobby McGee has won his last three starts all on Good ground at 1m — the step to 1m1f is the only question, but his current form makes him the horse everyone else must beat if he handles the trip.

Antigua ridden by Ryan Moore could dictate if he gets a clear lead or settles just behind Listentodwindblow; Moore's ability to manage a front-running horse under pressure in a contested pace scenario is the critical variable to watch in the first three furlongs.

How'sthebai has a worrying sim-going record on Good (1/5, no wins) and is heading into a three-way battle for the lead — if the ground is riding fast and the pace is fierce, this horse may empty badly in the straight.

Liberation Date ran only two days ago and arrives in poor form; watch for any signs of absence or non-participation on the day, and if she does run, monitor how she handles the early pace having had no recovery time.

The surplus of prominent-running types forced back — particularly Sanctijude and Anushka — means the midfield section will be congested early; watch for traffic problems on the straight run-in, especially for horses who need a gap to appear late.

races.name: Dubai Duty Free Irish European Breeders Fund Ragusa Handicap (Premier Handicap)

runners_data.name: Dawn Rising
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for JP O'Brien/Sheridan with strong recent Good-ground form over staying trips; 25 days since last run is fine at age 9, but needs a proper end-to-end gallop to produce his best late surge.
runners_data.comment: Familiar with today's ground and carrying experience in this grade, Dawn Rising heads our figures despite a below-par season to date; the 12f trip looks a shade short of his ideal range and a stronger showing is needed to justify favouritism.

runners_data.name: This Songisforyou
runners_data.note: 288 days off (23 jumps runs since) is a major concern for this Colin Keane-ridden hold-up type; useful Good-ground handicap form over 1m2f-1m6f but freshness after that layoff is genuinely unknown.
runners_data.comment: Consistent performer effective at today's trip, This Songisforyou has a top rider back on board after fading quickly following a series of errors in a maiden hurdle at Clonmel last time; his mark looks about right and he faces a stiff task.

runners_data.name: In My Teens
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the race, giving Gavin Cromwell's four-year-old total control of the pace; headgear worn, Good-ground form is acceptable, but the style-fit flag (0.93) reflects that this trip and company stretch its comfort zone.
runners_data.comment: Useful Flat performer with scope for further improvement at this longer trip, In My Teens was found wanting for pace when beaten seven lengths here last time; a first-time hood could help and she is open to progress, though the trainer's recent record is a note of caution.

runners_data.name: Cloud Seeker
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery trains and rides this prominent-style five-year-old; Good-ground form is mixed and stepping up from shorter trips means the 1m4f is the main query, though the trainer/jockey combination booking is intriguing.
runners_data.comment: Back on a workable mark and proven at today's trip and going, Cloud Seeker came back to form here last time beaten four lengths after a break; effective at 10-12f with an accessible weight, he merits respect in a wide-open field.

runners_data.name: The Real Screamer
runners_data.note: Paul Flynn's five-year-old arrives on a sharp upward curve (two consecutive wins), both over shorter trips at Leopardstown/Naas on Good or Soft; the step to 1m4f on fast ground is the sole unknown for this prominent-racing type.
runners_data.comment: On a hot streak with three wins in recent starts, The Real Screamer landed a handicap by four lengths at Leopardstown last time off a lower mark and continues to progress; now at a career-high official mark, the question is whether that momentum can be maintained.

runners_data.name: Marazion
runners_data.note: John Harrington's four-year-old has won at 1m2f on Good ground and placed at 1m4f; 14 days since last run is very tight but Shane Foley retains the ride and its progressive profile suits the controlled-pace scenario well.
runners_data.comment: Maiden winner who looked in good shape before stepping into Group company, Marazion was beaten six lengths in a Group 3 at Cork last time and returns to handicaps on what looks a fair mark; proven at today's trip on soft and good ground.

runners_data.name: Factual Fact
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's seven-year-old has been remarkably consistent in staying handicaps on Good and Heavy ground, finishing in the frame five times in its last five; Ronan Whelan takes the ride and the 1m4f trip is a proven stamina weapon.
runners_data.comment: Won at Killarney two starts back and ran a fine race last time despite missing the break and doing too much too soon, Factual Fact is in good form and effective at this trip; the 4lb rise makes life slightly harder but he remains very much in the mix.

runners_data.name: What's Your Game
runners_data.note: 90 days since last run for this Robson De Aguiar four-year-old is a flag; prominent style but Good-ground form is thin (sim-going only 0W1P), and stepping back up to 1m4f after disappointing runs brings questions.
runners_data.comment: Off a 90-day break and carrying a still-stiff mark, What's Your Game was taken too far forward over an extended trip at Navan on his return and failed to see it out; effective up to 13f on a variety of surfaces but needs a more patient ride here.

runners_data.name: Retracement
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's five-year-old is a genuine front-rank operator by inclination but, with so many prominent types present, is likely to find itself racing off the pace against its nature — Ben Coen will need to adapt quickly, and the style-fit flag (0.92) is worth heeding.
runners_data.comment: Faded late when beaten four lengths here last time after a break, Retracement is on a mark that looks about right; a trainer in form is a positive and today's ground suits, but he ranks towards the lower end of our figures and has more to prove.

runners_data.name: Star Harbour
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up type for Adrian McGuinness wearing a visor; Good-ground form record is modest (0W1P in similar conditions) and the eight-year-old has shown only brief flashes of form, making Adam Caffrey's task a difficult one.
runners_data.comment: Back in form at Carlisle last time when beaten just over two lengths off a slightly lower mark, Star Harbour is a capable veteran who handles today's going and distance; a first-time visor could help him focus and he merits respect despite a mixed recent strike rate.

runners_data.name: Obscenity
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle partners this improving JP O'Brien four-year-old that has won twice on Good ground at 1m-1m2f; genuinely front-running in nature but the crowded pace scenario means it is listed midfield — if it does secure prominent ground it could make a bold show.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in recent starts including a handicap at Gowran Park last time off a 9lb lower mark, Obscenity has been progressing steadily and tries a first-time visor here; effective at today's trip, he may have a little more in hand though he steps up in mark.

runners_data.name: Truth Be Told
runners_data.note: A natural front-rank horse by form who has won twice on Good ground at 1m-1m2f, but M C Grassick's four-year-old faces the same congestion problem at the head of affairs — 49 days off is not ideal, and it will need to find its position quickly with McCullagh aboard.
runners_data.comment: Won back-to-back in recent starts including a narrow success at Leopardstown last time after being forced to switch, Truth Be Told is still relatively unexposed at middle distances and has more to come; he sits at the foot of our figures and steps up in competition here.

runners_data.name: Navy Waters
runners_data.note: McCreery's five-year-old has smart placed form in staying handicaps on Good ground (3W5P overall) and wears a visor; another whose front-running inclination is squeezed by the competitive pace map, and 56 days off plus 22 jumps runs compounds the fitness question.
runners_data.comment: Progressive on the Flat and suited by today's trip, Navy Waters returns from a hurdles debut at Punchestown where she ran respectably; she has flat form to suggest she can be competitive but sits towards the lower end of our figures and faces an uphill task.

runners_data.name: Railwayview Lady
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan rides this four-year-old hold-up filly who wears a hood; has won on Good ground but history shows she is inconsistent (two 8ths in last two), and the step to 1m4f on fast ground stretches her proven stamina.
runners_data.comment: Beaten five lengths here last time and seemingly crying out for a stiffer test, Railwayview Lady steps up in trip today and tries first-time cheekpieces; effective at 10-12f on suitable ground and the longer distance is a plus, but the mark still looks stiff.

races.paceDynamic: In My Teens is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no significant challenger for the lead, will dictate from the front at a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over 1m4f at the Curragh. The pace is unlikely to be truly searching, meaning the race will be set up as a procession from the front with a single sustained burst in the straight rather than a genuine stamina examination. This race shape — controlled, moderate tempo, single pace-setter — strongly favours horses able to track closely or peel off a compact midfield group with a turn of foot, particularly those with proven form on Good to Firm. The field holds more genuine prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: Retracement, Truth Be Told, Obscenity and Navy Waters are all natural front-rank horses who are likely to find themselves shuffled into midfield positions against their nature, making their challenges harder to time; of these, Obscenity and Truth Be Told have the class and recent form to most plausibly secure a forward berth if any do.

watchPoints.text: In My Teens is the sole pace-setter — if Gary Carroll is allowed to dictate at a crawl unchallenged, the race could be run at an entirely false tempo that makes it impossible for hold-up horses to close.

Retracement, Truth Be Told and Obscenity are all natural front-runners who may be forced wider or further back than they want in the early stages — monitor them jostling for position in the first two furlongs, as that friction could compromise all three.

This Songisforyou returns after 287 days away (plus 23 jumps runs); even with Colin Keane aboard, a hold-up horse this far off a flat run is a significant fitness risk on a sharp Good to Firm surface.

The going report consistently reads Good to Firm across all nine races today — faster than the advertised Good — which will sharpen the demands on stamina in the closing stages and may particularly disadvantage horses without confirmed fast-ground form.

Marazion ran only 14 days ago; watch closely in the paddock and early running for any sign of jaded movement, as a quick turnaround at this level can be a positive (trainer form 6/37) or a fatigue signal.
